skill.name: variant
skill.description: Creates distinct UI component variants in the real page, adds a shareable picker, and presents tradeoffs for user selection.
skill.summary: Build and compare purposeful UI variants within the product context.

content.value_statement: Teams often compare superficial UI alternatives without learning which design decision matters. This skill builds distinct, accessible variants and a shareable picker for informed selection.
actual_capabilities: Scopes each run to one UI component and restates its purpose.
Reviews the project styling system, tokens, component library, and surrounding page.
Defines one primary design axis with distinct positions for each variant.
Builds three variants in the real page using realistic content.
Adds a URL-based picker with keyboard navigation and accessible state.
Presents tradeoffs, promotes the selected variant, and removes the temporary harness.
limitations: Focuses on one UI component per run, not an entire dashboard.
Requires project access to match existing styles, tokens, and context accurately.
Leaves the final choice to the user unless a recommendation is requested.
Provides a picker specification, but implementation details must fit the project framework.

use_cases.title: Compare Component Directions
use_cases.description: Build three meaningful versions of a component and evaluate them inside the production page.

use_cases.title: Review Design Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare structure, density, emphasis, typography, or voice without changing every variable.

use_cases.title: Test System Flexibility
use_cases.description: Explore component directions while preserving tokens, accessibility requirements, and established interface conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three variants of [component] on [page]. Use existing project styles, realistic content, and a picker. Summarize each tradeoff.

prompt_templates.title: Explore One Design Axis
prompt_templates.prompt: Build three [component] variants along the [structure, density, emphasis, type, or voice] axis. Keep accessibility and all secondary choices coherent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare deliberate positions on one design dimension.

prompt_templates.title: Iterate Around a Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Keep the existing variant harness. Create three new positions around [selected direction], preserve realistic data, and explain the refined tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a second exploration after initial feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Constrained Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: Build five variants of [component] within [constraints]. Test at [widths], verify interactions and accessibility, then provide shareable links and neutral tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate a wide design space under explicit product constraints.

output_examples.input: Create three account summary card variants focused on information density.
output: Quiet: generous spacing and reduced metadata for occasional review.
Balanced: moderate density with clear account status and next action.
Dense: compact rows and complete metadata for frequent operational use.

output_examples.input: Compare navigation header variants and explain their tradeoffs.
output_examples.output: The compact direction preserves workspace height but reduces label visibility. The expanded direction improves scanning but consumes more vertical space.

output_examples.input: Prepare shareable review details for the selected variants.
output: Picker location: fixed at the bottom center.
Each variant has a dedicated URL query parameter.

best_practices: Choose one primary design axis before implementation.
Use realistic content and evaluate variants inside the actual page.
Verify keyboard access, focus visibility, responsive layout, interactions, and console output.
anti_patterns: Do not create variants that differ only by color or copy.
Do not vary every design axis at the same time.
Do not keep the picker harness after promoting a production variant.

faq.question: How many variants does the skill create?
faq.answer: It creates three by default and may create five when requested or when the design space is broad.

faq.question: Does the skill choose the winning variant?
faq.answer: No. It presents neutral tradeoffs and leaves the decision to the user unless a recommendation is requested.

faq.question: Which design dimensions can vary?
faq.answer: The primary axis can be structure, density, emphasis, typography, or voice.

faq.question: How are variants selected?
faq.answer: A floating picker updates a URL search parameter and supports arrow keys and number keys.

faq.question: What accessibility requirements apply?
faq.answer: Every variant needs accessible names, keyboard operation, visible focus, responsive behavior, and meaning beyond color.

faq.question: What happens after a variant is selected?
faq.answer: The selected direction moves into the production component. The unused variants and temporary harness are removed.
